summary: 36 runs, all built on four shared helpers (polygon-set, shape-segments, topology-output, geometry-tree): a grid of 12 to 18 star-shaped shore polygons, one river reach, or the crossing river lines. The pictures are tidy, but most show many small copies of the same shape, so a card shows a texture more than an operation. 17 runs scrub a Data: knob, 11 scrub by full rebuild, and most of the real props (tolerance, gridSize, offsetDistance, ratio, distance) are WGSL constants fixed at construction. Pointer interaction here is mostly about geometry: drag a vertex or line (make-valid, polygonize, minimum bounds/clearance, inscribed circle), reach a tolerance ring (snaps, precision grids, offsets, concave hull), or move a window (bounds-filter, rectangle-clip, both already per-frame). Best pictures: ratio-concave-hull, rectangle-clip, line-precision-reduction, local-frame-projection, minimum-bounds, polygonize. Worst: geometry-cleanup (a nearly straight line, so nothing happens), convex-straight-skeleton (offset edges shoot to the world origin), lon-lat-polygon-preparation (everything squeezed into the top strip of a world map), and the two canonical-equality runs and normalize-geometry, whose effect cannot be seen at card size. Shared changes that would fix many entries at once: a drag-a-vertex helper and a proper fill triangulation in shared/polygon-set.ts, writable crossing-line positions so the four crossing-line runs can drag a line per frame, a geodesic-arc helper in shared/shape-segments.ts for the two geodesic runs, and a framework way to snap a rebuildOn parameter to a few prebuilt variants.

sharedChanges.change: Add a moveVertex(set, feature, vertex, point) helper that rewrites positions, outline and fill for one dragged vertex (smooth falloff to its neighbours), plus pointer-to-nearest-vertex lookup on the CPU set; this enables the drag archetype per frame.

The fill mesh is a triangle fan from the shell center: it ignores holes and spills outside bent (banana) shapes. Use an ear-clipping triangulation with holes so filled polygons match the geometry the operation sees.
Have createCrossingLines return a regenerate(offsets) function with fixed vertex counts, so one line can be shifted per frame with buffer.write instead of a rebuild.
Add addGeodesicArcs: sample N intermediate rows (k/N of the distance) with GPUGeodesicDestination and draw them as a polyline, so the map shows the real great-circle path instead of a straight chord.
createSingleLine picks a random river reach, and some reaches are almost straight (geometry-cleanup draws a flat line). Choose a fixed sinuous reach index, or reject reaches with low sinuosity.
Add addLatticeSegments(gridSize, bounds): a faint grid of the precision lattice drawn under the output, so precision reduction and cleanup show what the line is rounded to.

frameworkNeeds: pointer position in world coordinates with both x and y bound to a run callback (place, window, drag) instead of one parameter along x
pointer-to-nearest vertex, line or feature lookup on CPU inputs, with the picked id kept for the whole drag
cursor glyphs: ring of a given radius at the pointer or at a picked point, box outline, crosshair, vertical curtain line
per-feature highlight buffer on polygons and segments layers (probe of one ring, leaf or line)
small readback of per-feature values for the readout text (area, flags, clearance, distance) without a full afterRun
snap a rebuildOn parameter to N prebuilt graph variants (or debounce rebuilds) for WGSL-constant props: tolerance, gridSize, offsetDistance, ratio, distance
direction arrowheads on segments/paths layers so ring winding and start vertices can be seen
swipe curtain that clips context and output layers to either side of the pointer x
legend chips for categorical uint32 values (equal/not equal, valid/invalid classes, reversed/kept)
